channel.title: Startup Decoding — India's Premier Startup Media
channel.description: Startup stories, founder journeys, funding news and more from across India.

item.title: BazaarNow Raises ₹72 Crore Led by Peak XV — Quick Commerce Is Not Done Growing
item.description: Just as Zepto files for its IPO, BazaarNow closes a ₹72 crore round led by Peak XV Partners. The quick commerce space in India is getting more interesting by the week.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Zepto Files Updated DRHP — India's Quick Commerce Giant Is Ready for Dalal Street
item.description: Zepto filed its updated DRHP with SEBI on June 8, 2026 for a ₹8,010 crore fresh issue. With revenue doubling and losses widening, here's what you need to know before it lists.
item.author: Ishita Chaudhary (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Richa Kar Broke a Taboo — And Built a ₹500 Crore Business Doing It
item.description: When Richa Kar launched Zivame, India had no mainstream online lingerie platform. She didn't just build a business — she changed the conversation around women's bodies and shopping.
item.author: Sapna Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Vineeta Singh Built SUGAR Cosmetics by Saying No to a ₹1 Crore Job — And Won
item.description: She turned down a ₹1 crore placement offer from IIM Ahmedabad to start a beauty brand. A decade later, SUGAR Cosmetics is a household name and Vineeta Singh is one of India's most recognised founders.
item.author: Arshita Chaudhry (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: DPIIT Recognition — The First Step Every Indian Startup Must Take
item.description: DPIIT recognition is not just a certificate — it unlocks tax benefits, faster IP processing, government tenders, and more. Here's how to get it and why it matters.
item.author: SD Desk (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Atal Innovation Mission — How India Is Building a Culture of Innovation from School Onwards
item.description: From school tinkering labs to university incubators, the Atal Innovation Mission is building an innovation pipeline for India's next generation. Here's the full picture.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups — Get Loans Without the Collateral Headache
item.description: Banks have always been reluctant to lend to startups. The Credit Guarantee Scheme for Startups is trying to change that — here's how it works and who it's for.
item.author: SD Desk (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 — The Government Just Put ₹10,000 Crore on the Table
item.description: The Government of India has launched Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 with a massive ₹10,000 crore corpus. Here's what it means for Indian founders.
item.author: SD Desk (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Razorpay's 58,000 Crore Journey — How Two IIT Roorkee Friends Solved India's Payment Problem for Businesses
item.description: Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar were IIT Roorkee batchmates frustrated with how hard it was to accept online payments as a small business. They fixed it — and built a 58,000 crore company.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Ola Electric's IPO Story — Bhavish Aggarwal's Bold 50,000 Crore Bet on Making India the EV Capital of the World
item.description: Bhavish Aggarwal spent 11 years building Ola cabs. Then he pivoted completely — built the world's largest two-wheeler factory in 13 months, listed on Indian stock exchanges, and declared India will lead the global EV revolution.
item.author: Yash Rao (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Dream11 — How Harsh Jain Built India's Most Downloaded Sports App and a 65,000 Crore Empire From a College Idea **Category:** Startup Stories
item.description: Harsh Jain launched Dream11 in 2008 as a college project. For six years, it went nowhere. Then the IPL changed everything — and Dream11 became India's most downloaded app.
item.author: Gourav Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Startup India Seed Fund — The Government Is Giving 20 Lakh Grants to Early Stage Startups. Here's How to Apply
item.description: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme has ?945 crore earmarked for early-stage Indian startups. Grants of up to 20 lakh and loans of up to 50 lakh are available. Here is the complete guide.
item.author: SD Desk (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: MUDRA Yojana Has Given 27 Lakh Crore to Small Businesses. Here Is Your Complete Guide to Getting a Loan
item.description: Since 2015, MUDRA Yojana has disbursed over ?27 lakh crore to 40+ crore small business owners across India — with zero collateral required. Here is how you can access it.
item.author: SD Desk (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Zerodha's 70,000 Crore Secret — How Nithin Kamath Built India's Biggest Stockbroker Without a Single Rupee of Venture Capital
item.description: Every startup in India raised venture capital. Zerodha raised zero. Today it has 1.5 crore customers, 8,000+ crore revenue, and is India's largest stockbroker — all built without a single external investor.
item.author: Gourav Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: How Physics Wallah Became India's Most Affordable EdTech Unicorn — Alakh Pandey's 9,000 Crore Mission
item.description: Alakh Pandey was a teacher uploading free videos on YouTube from his bedroom. He refused to make education expensive. That refusal built Physics Wallah — India's most affordable edtech unicorn.
item.author: Yash Rao (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: OYO's 35,000 Crore Comeback — Ritesh Agarwal's Lesson in Resilience That Every Founder Needs to Hear
item.description: At 19, Ritesh Agarwal became Asia's youngest funded founder. At 26, OYO was on the edge of collapse. At 29, he led India's most dramatic startup comeback.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Lenskart's 33,000 Crore Disruption — Peyush Bansal Fixed an Industry Nobody Thought Was Broken
item.description: Before Lenskart, buying glasses in India meant visiting dusty local opticians with limited choices at high prices. Peyush Bansal changed the entire experience — and built a 33,000 crore company.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Nykaa — The Story of Falguni Nayar, a 49-Year-Old Banker Who Became India's Richest Self-Made Woman
item.description: At 49, Falguni Nayar had everything — a prestigious career, financial security, professional respect. She quit it all to sell lipstick online. At 58, her company listed at ?1 lakh crore.
item.author: Arshita Chaudhry (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: PhonePe's 14,500 Crore Story — How Sameer Nigam Saw What Everyone Else Missed in UPI.
item.description: In 2015, Sameer Nigam and two colleagues quit Flipkart to build PhonePe on an unproven system called UPI. Today PhonePe has 60 crore users, processes 770 crore transactions a month, and is valued at $14.5 billion.
item.author: Gourav Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Meesho's 32,000 Crore Bet on India's Small Towns — Why Everyone Else Got Bharat Wrong.
item.description: While every startup chased metro India, Meesho went after housewives and small town sellers on WhatsApp. That contrarian bet created India's fastest-growing e-commerce company.
item.author: Yash Rao (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: Mamaearth — How Varun and Ghazal Alagh Turned a Baby Product Problem into a 10,000 Crore Listed Company
item.description: When Varun and Ghazal couldn't find safe products for their newborn, they started making their own with 5,000. That kitchen experiment is now India's first D2C unicorn — listed on stock exchanges.
item.author: Arshita Chaudhry (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: CRED's Unusual Strategy — How Kunal Shah Built a 20,000 Crore Startup by Rejecting Millions of Indians.
item.description: CRED said no to 99% of Indians. Only credit card users with a score above 750 could join. That extreme exclusivity is exactly what made it worth 20,000 Crore
item.author: Gourav Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)

item.title: How Two Teenagers Built Zepto — India's Fastest Grocery Delivery Startup Now Worth $7 Billion
item.description: Two 18-year-old school friends from Mumbai dropped out of Stanford, came back to India during COVID, and built a $7 billion grocery delivery giant in just 4 years.
item.author: Anup Yadav (yadavgourav634@gmail.com)
